target.title: fix(openai): repair stale doctor route pins
target.body:
Closes #101672

AI-assisted.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose sessions automatically fell back to canonical `openai` could keep stale OpenAI model/provider routing state after running `openclaw doctor --fix --deep`, because doctor had no OpenAI session-route owner for the literal `openai` provider id.

## Why This Change Was Made

This uses the existing plugin doctor contract seam instead of adding a new repair path: the OpenAI plugin now declares ownership of canonical `openai` session route state, while Codex keeps ownership of legacy Codex ids such as `openai-codex`. The generic session-route repair also clears fallback-origin provenance when it clears an auto model override, so doctor does not leave stale provenance after reporting the route state repaired.

## User Impact

Operators can expect `doctor --fix --deep` to detect and clear stale auto-created `openai` session route pins after defaults move back to a non-OpenAI primary, without hand-patching installed plugin files or manually editing session JSON. Explicit/user model choices still go through the existing manual-review path rather than being silently cleared.

## Evidence

Exact head: `16e3396ecad7b41324a7dc43d311dd0e24091d0d`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-state-providers.test.ts extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` passed after the rebase: 2 Vitest shards, 14 tests.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint src/commands/doctor-session-state-providers.ts src/commands/doctor-session-state-providers.test.ts extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` passed after the rebase.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/commands/doctor-session-state-providers.ts src/commands/doctor-session-state-providers.test.ts extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` passed after the rebase.
- `git diff --check` passed after the rebase.
- `OPENCLAW_HOME=<tmp>/home OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/openclaw.json HOME=<tmp>/home corepack pnpm openclaw config validate --json` returned `{"valid":true}` for the fixture config.
- Real fixture-backed CLI proof: `OPENCLAW_HOME=<tmp>/home OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/openclaw.json HOME=<tmp>/home corepack pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --deep --non-interactive --yes` completed successfully.
  - Before doctor: `sessionId` was `sess-stale-openai`, `updatedAt` was `1`, and these stale fields were present: `providerOverride`, `modelOverride`, `modelOverrideSource`, `modelOverrideFallbackOriginProvider`, `modelOverrideFallbackOriginModel`, `modelProvider`, `model`, `contextTokens`, `fallbackNoticeActiveModel`, `fallbackNoticeReason`, `authProfileOverride`, `authProfileOverrideSource`, `authProfileOverrideCompactionCount`.
  - Doctor output included: `Found stale OpenAI session routing state in 1 session outside the current configured model/runtime route.` and `Cleared stale OpenAI session routing state for 1 session.`
  - After doctor: `sessionId` was still `sess-stale-openai`, `updatedAt` was updated to a current timestamp, and all 13 stale fields listed above were absent.
- Earlier additional seam validation before the rebase also passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/doctor-contract-registry.test.ts`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/bundled-plugin-metadata.test.ts test/scripts/bundled-plugin-build-entries.test.ts`, and `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (`autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`). The diff was then rebased cleanly and the touched-surface proof above was rerun on exact head.
- Upstream Codex source checked locally: `codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs` defines `OPENAI_PROVIDER_ID` as `openai`, builds the built-in OpenAI provider with Responses wire API and OpenAI auth, includes `openai` in built-in providers, and merges user-configured providers without replacing the built-in `openai` entry.

What was not tested: a live paid-provider doctor run against a production session store; the regression is covered by focused tests plus a real fixture-backed `openclaw doctor --fix --deep` CLI run without external credentials.
